phase3_findings.description: docs/internal/mcp-server/transport.md:120 says a call cancelled while queued never runs, and the run_memory_call docstring says a caller cancelled before its call starts drops it; asyncio.wrap_future cancels the executor future from a call_soon-scheduled done callback, so the single worker can start the queued call in that gap.
Test stubs (_StoreCalls._enter, _held_call, held_iter_all) ignore the return value of held.wait(HOLD_LIMIT_S), so a hold timeout is not reported.

store.py executor rationale comment gives only the object.__new__ test reason, omits that server.py builds two MemoryStore instances, and names a 'store's own executor' MemoryStore does not have (it is ChromaAgentMemory's).
transport.md:119 names 'the store's own two-thread executor' (it is ChromaAgentMemory's) and says last_skipped_rows is shared by every caller, which holds only per instance.
The one-store-call-at-a-time rule is enforced only by convention; MemoryStore's synchronous methods remain public and callable from any thread.
run_memory_call's Callable[P, T] -> T signature accepts generator functions, lazy iterators and async callables whose store work would not run on the worker.
_baseline docstring guarantee is accurate but does not cover async per-entry writes on ChromaAgentMemory's executor, ordered only by the handlers' asyncio.Locks.
Overlap test covers only export/list/stats; import_bundle's baseline and clear_memories are never run concurrently with a read tool.
No test checks that a call cancelled while waiting in the memory worker queue is dropped.
The 'never runs' cancellation claim in transport.md:120 and the run_memory_call docstring is absolute though a race window exists between task cancel and the wrap_future done callback.
Loop-side test replaces server_module.json with a namespace holding only dumps and asserts exactly seven calls, which is brittle to future json use.

report:
## Verdict: APPROVE with notes (only Suggestion findings; all 34 checklist items passed)
The PR is ready to merge: the memory tools' synchronous store calls now run one at a time on a single worker thread, every acceptance criterion passed verification, and no reviewer found a Critical or Important defect.
Rule applied: rule 6 — only findings below the critical threshold remain → APPROVE with notes

## Code Review Findings

### 🟡 Suggestion / Minor (10)

<details><summary>10 items</summary>

1. `docs/internal/mcp-server/transport.md` line 120 says "A call cancelled while it waits in the queue never runs", and the `run_memory_call` docstring in `src/sqllens/memory/store.py` (lines 102-104) says "A caller cancelled before its call starts drops it". Both are absolute, but `asyncio.wrap_future` cancels the thread-pool future from a done callback that asyncio schedules with `call_soon`. If the single worker takes the queued item in that gap, the call runs anyway and is then logged as finished after cancel. Write "normally never runs" or describe the window. (raised by 2/6 agents) <!-- inertness: first-conjunct=held limb-one=held limb-two=held; evidence: rewording changes no output or branch; git grep of *.sh *.py *.jq *.yml CLAUDE.md AGENTS.md .claude/ .prflow/skill-extensions/ for "never runs" and "drops it" found only the prose itself and an unrelated SQL pool docstring; internal doc page and a never-printed docstring -->
2. `tests/unit/test_memory_event_loop.py` line 440 (`_StoreCalls._enter`), `_held_call` near line 675, and `held_iter_all` in `tests/integration/test_memory_tool_responsiveness.py` line 36 ignore the return value of `held.wait(HOLD_LIMIT_S)`, so a hold that times out continues silently and the failure message is less clear. (raised by 1/6 agents)
3. `src/sqllens/memory/store.py` lines 70-74: the comment explaining the module-level executor gives only a test reason (`object.__new__`) and leaves out the real one: `server.py` builds two `MemoryStore` instances (lines 412 and 501), so a per-instance executor would let import and admin calls overlap. It also names "the store's own executor", but `MemoryStore` has no executor; the two-thread executor belongs to `ChromaAgentMemory`. (raised by 1/6 agents) <!-- inertness: first-conjunct=held limb-one=held limb-two=held; evidence: rewording changes no output or branch; git grep of *.sh *.py *.jq *.yml CLAUDE.md AGENTS.md .claude/ .prflow/skill-extensions/ for "store's own" found only this comment; source comment never printed -->
4. `docs/internal/mcp-server/transport.md` line 119 also says "the store's own two-thread executor", which belongs to `ChromaAgentMemory`, not `MemoryStore`. Its "`last_skipped_rows` is shared by every caller" holds only per instance; the import path and the admin tools use different instances, so the single process-wide thread is what keeps them apart. (raised by 1/6 agents) <!-- inertness: first-conjunct=held limb-one=held limb-two=held; evidence: rewording changes no output or branch; git grep of *.sh *.py *.jq *.yml CLAUDE.md AGENTS.md .claude/ .prflow/skill-extensions/ for "store's own" found no tool or agent reader; internal doc page -->
5. `src/sqllens/memory/store.py` lines 70-116: the "one store call at a time" rule is kept only by convention. `MemoryStore`'s synchronous methods stay public, so a future async caller could call them directly or through `asyncio.to_thread` and bring back both loop blocking and overlap with no type or runtime check. (raised by 1/6 agents)
6. `src/sqllens/memory/store.py` lines 99-116: `run_memory_call` is typed `Callable[P, T] -> T` with no limit, so a generator function or lazy iterator (such as `MemoryStore.iter_records`) or an `async def` would be accepted, and its store work would run wherever the result is consumed. No current caller does this. (raised by 1/6 agents)
7. `src/sqllens/memory/importer.py` lines 36-41: the `_baseline` docstring's "no other call routed through `run_memory_call`" guarantee is accurate but does not cover the async per-entry writes, which run on `ChromaAgentMemory`'s own executor and are ordered only by the handlers' `asyncio.Lock`s. (raised by 1/6 agents)
8. `tests/unit/test_memory_event_loop.py` lines 563-580: the overlap test runs only `export_memories`, `list_memories` and `get_memory_stats`; no test runs `import_bundle`'s baseline (`add_memories`, `import_memory`) or `clear_memories` concurrently with a read tool, so moving one of those paths off the single worker would still pass. (raised by 1/6 agents)
9. `src/sqllens/memory/store.py` lines 102-104: no test checks that a call cancelled while waiting in the queue is dropped; the tests cover only a call that has already started, unlike the SQL pool's matching "never runs a call cancelled while waiting" test. (raised by 1/6 agents)
10. `tests/unit/test_memory_event_loop.py` lines 638-664: the loop-side test replaces `server_module.json` with a namespace holding only `dumps` and asserts exactly seven calls, so any added `json` use on these paths breaks it even when behavior is correct. (raised by 1/6 agents)

</details>

acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] No call to a synchronous (non-`async`) `MemoryStore` method made by an MCP tool registered under `memory.allow_admin_tools` or `memory.allow_import` runs on the event-loop thread. A test records the thread each such call runs on, for every one of those tools, and asserts it is not the thread running the event loop.
- [ ] While a memory tool's store call is held open, `GET /healthz` on the same HTTP server returns 200 within 2 seconds, measured by a 2-second httpx request timeout as in `tests/integration/test_slow_agent_run_responsiveness.py`. Once released, the held tool call returns its normal, non-error result.
- [ ] Within one server process, synchronous (non-`async`) `MemoryStore` method calls made for two different calls of those MCP tools are never in progress at the same time. This holds even when the tool call that started one is cancelled while it runs: the next such call starts only after the cancelled call's store work returns.
- [ ] For the same store contents and arguments, with no write other than the call's own overlapping it and no cancellation of the call, each of those MCP tools returns the same result as before the change, including each `isError` result and message. That covers, at minimum, a memory that is not found, a corrupt store, invalid input, a lossy export, an add or import with failed items, and a generic store failure. A `list_memories` call whose store reads a managed write (a write inside `CollectionState.writing()`) overlaps returns an `isError` result whose text contains `Memory store changed during listing; retry the request.` and never a partial listing. The existing memory tool tests pass without changes to their assertions.
- [ ] The CLI `import-memory` command reports the same saved, duplicate and error counts and exit status as before for the same store and bundle, including with `--clear` and `--dry-run`.
- [ ] The change leaves `add_memories`' per-item validation, `import_memory`'s parsing of its bundle JSON, `import_bundle`'s per-item de-duplication check of the incoming items, and each handler's final `json.dumps` of the object its `memory.admin` function returns running on the event loop.
